After months of testing Liquid Glass, WhatsApp is expanding the rollout of its redesigned iPad app interface, including a new Mac-like sidebar. Here's everything you need to know.

WhatsApp is working on a new iPad app interface

While WhatsApp first began adapting its iOS app to the Liquid Glass visual overhaul back in October, it took the company several months before bringing this redesign to the iPad, with limited beta testing beginning in June.

WABetaInfo reported at the time that the redesign brought Liquid Glass-styled tabs, buttons, and contextual menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar used on iPhone.

According to a new report from WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now rolling out another major interface change for some iPad users, replacing the bottom tab bar by default with a new Mac-like sidebar.

The sidebar mirrors the layout of the existing WhatsApp for Mac, providing quick access to chats, status updates, communities, calls, Meta AI, and other parts of the app. Users can also hide the sidebar to give more room to the chat list and conversation window.

From the report:

WABetaInfo says the new sidebar is now available to some beta testers running the latest TestFlight build, though some users on the regular App Store version are also starting to see the new interface.

As is typical with WhatsApp rollouts, it will take some time before the new interface reaches all users, whether they're on the beta or the stable version of the app. Once it does, however, iPad users will benefit from a layout that's better suited to the tablet form factor.
